subject: Liability cushion and liquidated damages request from Atlas Health
messages:
From: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlashealth.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: stronger financial remedies (LDs / termination rights)

Rafael / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the latency characteristics look promising for our clinician-facing workflows. Before we can present Redwood to our board and procurement committee, we need clearer contractual remedies for sustained outages and severe latency regressions. Our procurement and legal teams are pushing for: 

- Liquidated damages (LDs) for recurring SLO breaches with a defined per-month cap;
- A limited fee-at-risk tranche (5–10% of committed spend) held in escrow for the initial 12 months;
- Explicit termination rights if service availability falls below 95% for two consecutive months after cure.

I've attached a redline of our standard terms where we've highlighted the clauses we want to see adjusted. We recognize Redwood's position on commercial risk — we're open to a capped, staged approach rather than an open-ended penalty. Can you review and let us know what is feasible?

Attachments: Atlas_Redwood_Redline_20261123.pdf (redline)

Best,
Sofia Reyes
Sr. Procurement Manager, Atlas Health
sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: stronger financial remedies (LDs / termination rights)

Sofia — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the redline. Appreciated.

High level: we want Atlas to feel comfortable with reliability guarantees, but we also need to avoid asymmetric exposure that could jeopardize our ability to serve all customers. A few initial thoughts we can offer quickly:

- We can consider a small escrow / fee-at-risk tranche tied to committed spend for the first 12 months, with staged release based on monthly SLOs;
- Rather than open-ended LDs, we prefer a severity-indexed compensation model (credits + capped cash remedy) with a hard quarterly cap (e.g., 10% of quarterly committed fees).
- Termination for repeated breaches is something we can discuss if there's no cure after formal remediation steps; we generally ask for a 30–60 day cure window and operational remediation plan.

I'll loop Marissa and Legal to draft counter language that preserves a cure pathway while offering Atlas commercial comfort. Can you confirm whether the redline's proposed 95% availability trigger is for production (multi-region) traffic or for a single-region deployment? That affects how we shape the remedy.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: stronger financial remedies (LDs / termination rights)

Sofia — looping Legal and Sales Ops. Rafael: tagging Ben because he owns committed capacity economics.

Action plan from Redwood:
1) Rishi to propose alternative wording that preserves Atlas' ability to escrow a small percentage of committed fees while adding a cure/remediation ladder.
2) Ben and I will run numbers for a capped quarterly cash remedy and a staged release schedule for the escrow tranche.
3) We will return a redlined counter that keeps the core SLO definitions but tightens the operational triggers (per-region vs global) so the remedy is proportional.

Attached is the Atlas redline you shared. Expect our counter by EOD Fri.

Attachments: Atlas_Redwood_Redline_20261123.pdf

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood counter: LDs, escrow, and termination — proposed language

Sofia, team — thanks for patience. We've drafted a focused set of changes that aim to balance Atlas' need for contractual certainty with Redwood's operational realities. Summary of proposed approach (attached as a clean doc + markup):

- Escrow / Fee-at-risk: Redwood will agree to place up to 7.5% of the first 12 months' committed fees into an escrow mechanism administered by a mutually agreed third party. Funds are released monthly based on meeting monthly SLO thresholds; a partial release schedule is described in the attachment.

- Liquidated Damages: Replace open-ended LDs with a graduated remedy tied to severity and recurrence. For Severity 1 (total outage impacting >50% of production requests): credits for month 1; for repeated Severity 1 within a rolling 3-month window, a cash remedy up to 5% of monthly committed fees for that month, subject to a quarterly cap of 12% of quarterly committed fees.

- Termination: Customer may exercise termination rights only after: (a) two consecutive months of SLOs below the agreed threshold AND (b) Redwood fails to cure within a 45-day remediation plan approved by both parties. If termination is exercised in accordance with these steps, customer may receive a pro-rata refund of pre-paid but unused fees minus the escrowed amounts as described.

- Cap and Carve-outs: Remedies exclude breaches caused by force majeure, customer misconfiguration, and third-party network outages outside Redwood's control. Redwood proposes a mutual cap on aggregate remedies set at 30% of 12 months' committed fees (commercial cap).

Attached: Redwood_counter_LD_clause_20261127.docx (draft language and rationale). Happy to walk through line-by-line on a call.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Chief Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@atlashealth.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@atlashealth.io>, procurement@atlashealth.io
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood counter: LDs, escrow, and termination — proposed language

Team — thanks for the thoughtful counter and for putting a concrete escrow percentage on the table. A few quick points from Procurement / Legal at Atlas: 

1) The 7.5% escrow is directionally acceptable, but we need clarity on the escrow admin and dispute resolution if a release is contested.
2) The quarterly cap (12%) is lower than our ask; we'd prefer a 15% quarterly cap or a mechanism to increase the cap in the second year if service stabilizes — can Redwood consider a step-up model?
3) The 45-day cure period is workable provided the remediation plan includes specific milestones and executive escalation points.

Next step: we can accept the draft language as a redline baseline if Redwood is willing to: (a) add escrow admin details (third-party custodian + dispute process), and (b) agree to a step-up to 15% quarterly cap in year 2 if Atlas completes a usage milestone (e.g., 50% of committed throughput).

I've attached our procurement approval matrix showing who needs to sign at each step. If you can incorporate the two items above and send a final redline, I can escalate to our CFO for sign-off by mid-December. If not, we will need to escalate internally and pull in executive sponsorship.

Attachments: Procurement_approval_matrix.pdf

Thanks — Andrew
Andrew Cole
VP, Procurement | Atlas Health
andrew.cole@atlashealth.io
